title: Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal
subtitle: Warm spiced oat squares with tender apple chunks for easy portioning.
description: Steel-cut and rolled oats bake with diced apples, cinnamon, and brown sugar into sliceable squares—more satisfying than instant packets and easier to serve than stovetop porridge for ten. Holds warm in the oven between waves of eaters.

ingredients.name: chopped walnuts

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a 9x13 baking dish. Toss diced apples with half the cinnamon and spread in the bottom of the dish. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mix the oat base
steps.instruction: Whisk oats, milk, eggs, brown sugar, remaining cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt until combined. The mixture should look like thick pourable batter. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Pour and top
steps.instruction: Pour oat mixture over apples and scatter walnuts on top. Tap the dish to settle the batter evenly for uniform slices. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake until the center is set, edges are golden, and a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean. The top should spring back lightly when pressed. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 38 minutes for this step at crew scale.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Serve warm with maple syrup and optional butter pats. Hold uncovered at 200°F for up to 30 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Dice apples and mix batter while the oven preheats—this bake is forgiving on timing.
Cut squares in the pan with a sharp knife wiped between cuts for clean portions.
Set maple and walnuts at the line so customization doesn't bottleneck the hot squares.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 in warm water immediately—baked oatmeal cement is easier to release when warm.
Line the prep bowl with a thin film of oil before mixing sticky oat batter for faster cleanup.
leftovers: Wrap squares individually and reheat at 325°F for 10 minutes with a splash of milk on top.
Crumble cold squares into a skillet with butter and pan-fry until crisp for oatmeal hash browns.
